root_cause.text: biovec_phys_mergeable() in the block layer merged physically contiguous bio_vec segments based only on address contiguity and ignored whether their bv_page pages came from different dev_pagemaps, allowing zone-device bvecs from distinct pgmaps to be coalesced into a segment whose correct pgmap could no longer be determined.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `if (!zone_device_pages_have_same_pgmap(vec1->bv_page, vec2->bv_page)) return false;` to `biovec_phys_mergeable()`, and the CVE/commit message states that without this check, physically contiguous bvecs from different dev_pagemaps were coalesced, “making it impossible to recover the correct pgmap for the merged segment via page_pgmap().”

agent_logs.root_cause_candidate: biovec_phys_mergeable() in the block layer merged physically contiguous bio_vec segments based only on address contiguity and ignored whether their bv_page pages came from different dev_pagemaps, allowing zone-device bvecs from distinct pgmaps to be coalesced into a segment whose correct pgmap could no longer be determined.
agent_logs.evidence_points: The patch adds `if (!zone_device_pages_have_same_pgmap(vec1->bv_page, vec2->bv_page)) return false;` to `biovec_phys_mergeable()`, and the CVE/commit message states that without this check, physically contiguous bvecs from different dev_pagemaps were coalesced, “making it impossible to recover the correct pgmap for the merged segment via page_pgmap().”

intent_record.intent_summary: Prevent biovec physical merges across different zone-device pgmaps by rejecting adjacent pages that do not share the same pgmap.
intent_record.what: A new conditional check was added to biovec_phys_mergeable() after the adjacent-address test: if zone_device_pages_have_same_pgmap(vec1->bv_page, vec2->bv_page) returns false, the function now returns false.
intent_record.how: At runtime, physically adjacent biovecs are no longer considered mergeable when their pages belong to different zone device page maps, preventing merges across incompatible device-backed memory regions even if the addresses are contiguous.

grouping_result.intent: Prevent biovec physical merges across different zone-device pgmaps by rejecting adjacent pages that do not share the same pgmap.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly addresses the root cause by preventing physical bio_vec merges when adjacent pages belong to different zone-device dev_pagemaps/pgmaps, which is exactly the missing check that caused the vulnerability.

candidates.rationale: This contiguity-only check embodies the root cause: it permits merging based solely on adjacent physical addresses, without validating that the two bv_page pages belong to the same dev_pagemap.
This shows the function had a special-case mergeability check only for Xen, but no analogous check for differing zone-device pgmaps, leaving non-Xen merges to rely only on address adjacency.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement makes physical mergeability depend on address contiguity alone. As described in the root cause, that allowed bio_vecs backed by different dev_pagemaps to be merged when their addresses were adjacent, losing the ability to determine the correct pgmap for the merged segment.

This statement highlights that the code had a special mergeability validation only for Xen environments. Outside that special case, no equivalent check prevented merging adjacent zone-device pages from different dev_pagemaps, contributing to the vulnerable behavior.

Specifically, it computes `addr1 = bvec_to_phys(vec1)` and `addr2 = bvec_to_phys(vec2)`, then allows merging if `addr1 + vec1->bv_len == addr2`, `ARCH_BIOVEC_PHYS_MERGEABLE(vec1, vec2)` is true, and the segment boundary test `(addr1 | mask) == ((addr2 + vec2->bv_len - 1) | mask)` passes.
